text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: HelioDyne VPC — possible cross-tenant collateral exposure detected in dedicated pool helio-prod-3. Trigger: KV cache hit with anomalous namespace shims. Pager to oncall and security.
Alex L: saw the pager. quick summary: a Helio request returned cached KV entries that were tagged with a different tenant prefix. Suspicion: routing late-bind + cache prefix aliasing.
Maya R: oncall here, I've put helio-prod-3 into read-only routing via the router flag. Will start collecting traces. :white_check_mark:
Eli SRE: grabbing logs from the pod group. running `kubectl -n inference logs -l pool=helio-prod-3 --since=15m` now. any known recent deploys? 
Alex L: we pushed a small routing optimization 12m ago that introduced late-binding of tenant -> pool. It should be backwards compatible but might have missed prefix normalization.
Sophia (Security): tagging security. Important: treat as potential data exposure until proven otherwise. Need scope: how many customers impacted? any PII seen?
Cassie CSM: I've opened a private channel with HelioDyne CSM and account lead. They are on standby for an update. Please flag if we need to send an incident notification.
Oncall-June: I can take lead on live mitigation. Proposal: 1) Evict helio-prod-3 from serving (drain), 2) Invalidate KV prefix cache for that pool, 3) Roll back the routing change, 4) Snapshot evidence for forensics.
Alex L: agree. Adding steps: run `rctl pool isolate --pool helio-prod-3 --mode drain` then `rctl kvcache purge --pool helio-prod-3 --prefix '*' --reason "suspected-collateral-exposure"`.
DevOps-Bot: command queued: `rctl pool isolate --pool helio-prod-3 --mode drain` — started (job id 98f3). Estimated time to drain ~90s.
Eli SRE: logs show these entries around T-9m: ```
[2026-03-15T02:12:14Z] pool=helio-prod-3 req_id=abcd1234 tenant=helio user=svc-helio GET /kv key=customer_42/session-xyz cache_hit=true cache_key=ns:customer_99:session-xyz
```
Eli SRE: cache_key payload contained base64 user metadata that maps to customer_99. So indeed cache key contains mismatched tenant id.
Maya R: running a grep across recent clusters for `cache_key=ns:` to find other pools with similar entries.
Sophia (Security): collect a copy of the exact cached payload (redact sensitive fields) and hold it in secure evidence bucket. Also need to freeze any automated retention/eviction until we finish triage.
Alex L: hypothesis: our prefix normalization step was short-circuited by the late-binding change — when a request arrives it sometimes reassigns the tenant prefix after cache key computation, resulting in stale prefix in the cache. That would cause cross-tenant lookups.
Oncall-June: mitigation plan executed in parallel: - Pool isolation in progress (DevOps-Bot job id 98f3). - Purging keys from pool cache once drained. - Rolling back routing change through canary control plane: `deployctl rollback route-latebind --to-tag v2.4.1`.
DevOps-Bot: `rctl kvcache purge` queued (job id 98f4). Will run after drain completes.
Cassie CSM: HelioDyne asked whether their data might have been seen by others. For now they want a holding statement. Suggest: "We detected anomalous cache behavior affecting a dedicated pool; we've isolated the pool and are doing a scoped investigation. No confirmed customer-visible data leakage at this time." Approve?
Sophia (Security): approved as preliminary, but add: "We are treating this as a potential exposure and will notify customers if we confirm cross-tenant access."
Eli SRE: drain completed. DevOps-Bot shows job 98f3 finished. Purge job 98f4 running. I'll snapshot the cache and provide hashes to security.
Alex L: rolling back route-latebind now. `deployctl rollback route-latebind --to-tag v2.4.1 --reason "mitigation: preserve prefix normalization"` — starting.
Maya R: grep results show isolated occurrences limited to helio-prod-3 and one recent canary host in helio-prod-2. I'll mark helio-prod-2 canaries and force full key normalization check there.
Sophia (Security): we need an evidence manifest: list of affected request ids, sample payloads (redacted), cache keys, and timestamps. Eli/Maya please drop into the secure evidence bucket `s3://redwood-incidents/2143650000-helio-evidence/` and DM me the access link. Do not post payloads in slack.
Eli SRE: uploaded manifest (sha256:0bf3f9...). DMing security with access ACL. Also collected heap profiles from the runtime for Helio pods.
DevOps-Bot: purge job 98f4 complete. `rctl kvcache purge` returned 12,432 keys removed from helio-prod-3. 
Oncall-June: rolling forward: 1) keep helio-prod-3 isolated until we have security sign-off, 2) run a read-only run for Helio to verify behavior on a test replica, 3) patch code path to compute prefix after tenant resolution.
Alex L: I'll open a PR with fix and a test that asserts cache key contains final tenant id after routing decisions. Link when ready.
Cassie CSM: customer update: Sent holding statement to HelioDyne. They requested ETA for full report and whether they should rotate any keys. Recommend telling them to rotate any short-lived session tokens and we'll confirm if token material was included in cached payloads.
Sophia (Security): agree on rotation if sessions were in cached payloads. We will confirm. Also recommend legal loop-in if PII exposure confirmed.
Maya R: final note: there were no ingress spikes or attacks noted. Seems internally introduced. Good to know.
Alex L: thanks team. Next steps owners: Eli (evidence & logs), Sophia (scope & legal), Alex (code fix), Maya (host sweep), Cassie (customer comms). We'll reconvene in 30m unless any new findings.
incident-bot: Incident thread created. Severity: P2 -> elevated to P1 if evidence of confirmed cross-tenant access. Paging suppressed for 30m while we work on containment.
Oncall-June: handing off to night team in 25m. If any security confirms exposure escalate immediately and trigger customer notification workflow.
